name: Gastr del Sol
label: Drag City
lede: [[David Grubbs]] started in Louisville hardcore and moved to Chicago for graduate school. He named his next band half for his old one and half for a Derby winner, then spent five years taking rock songs apart with [[Jim O'Rourke]] until the two stopped working together.

eras.title: From Squirrel Bait to Bastro
eras.text: David Grubbs came up in Louisville's teenage punk scene, then moved his loud power trio to Chicago for graduate school. By 1991 he was tired of playing the same sound every night, and Gastr del Sol was his way out.

years.cap: Grubbs on stage with Squirrel Bait, 1985
years.h: Three high-school friends start Squirrelbait Youth on Halloween
years.p: [[Squirrel Bait|5dbf117b-c076-4d3b-b7ae-13517c25b2cf]] begins with [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]] on guitar, Clark Johnson on bass and Rich Schuler on drums. [[Brian McMahan|bebfec95-35a3-4cc8-b85e-8b178d09526d]] joins later and goes on to form [[Slint|2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28]].
years.xp:
Peter Searcy took over vocals by 1984, with Britt Walford on drums and McMahan on second guitar. The band put out an EP in 1985, the single "Kid Dynamite" in 1986 and the album Skag Heaven on Homestead Records in 1987.

It broke up in 1988 as the members scattered to college. McMahan and Walford formed Slint; Johnson became a lawyer.

years.cap: Squirrel Bait on a Jockey Club bill with Big Black and Urge Overkill, May 26, 1985
years.h: Bastro picks up where Squirrel Bait left off
years.p: [[Bastro|cfc5b1bf-a46c-4504-bcb6-a820416a1894]] is a post-hardcore power trio: Grubbs, ex-Squirrel Bait bassist Clark Johnson, and later drummer [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]] of My Dad Is Dead. Three albums follow on Homestead Records.
years.xp: The sound stayed loud and tight for three albums. Grubbs later told Paris Transatlantic that by the end, "it was always the same sound."

years.h: Bastro loses its bassist to law school
years.p: Clark Johnson quits for law school. [[Bundy K. Brown|940101f1-79c7-40ac-98d3-7b924b244a8e]] joins [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]] and [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]], and the last Bastro shows already sketch Gastr del Sol songs.
years.xp:
Grubbs told Paris Transatlantic the group needed a new way of working: "I went back to playing piano and took up the acoustic guitar."

Live tapes from those final shows came out in 2005 as Antlers: Live 1991 on Grubbs's Blue Chopsticks label.

eras.title: A racehorse name and two departures
eras.text: The trio rearranged Bastro's instrumentals for acoustic instruments and took a name that sounded foreign and wasn't. Then Tortoise pulled away Bundy K. Brown and John McEntire, and a Chicago guitarist asked his way in.

years.big: "Some sort of associative blending of the two."
years.h: Grubbs names the band for Bastro and a racehorse
years.p: Gato del Sol won the 1982 Kentucky Derby, the same year Squirrel Bait started in Louisville. Grubbs told Paris Transatlantic how the two names fused.

Gastr del Sol's debut was recorded September to November 1992 in Chicago and Minneapolis with [[Brian Paulson|65f13d3b-ddd6-4b33-8ab7-366ee7fb63c4]]. [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]] and [[Bundy K. Brown|940101f1-79c7-40ac-98d3-7b924b244a8e]] wrote all eight songs.
years.xp: It came out on TeenBeat Records, the D.C.-area label run by [[Unrest|f444dc7d-59c1-4ed6-beb7-f90b6d85366c]]'s Mark Robinson. Drag City reissued it on June 16, 1997.

years.h: Tortoise takes Bundy K. Brown and John McEntire
years.p: [[Bundy K. Brown|940101f1-79c7-40ac-98d3-7b924b244a8e]] and [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]] put their time into [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]]. McEntire keeps playing on Gastr records and touring with them.

years.h: Jim O'Rourke wanted a rock band, then heard the debut
years.p: O'Rourke first wanted a heavy guitar band and early rehearsals flopped. Then The Serpentine Similar came out and he asked in; by October he's recording Crookt, Crackt, or Fly.
years.xp:
Grubbs told Paris Transatlantic how it started: "Jim called me to ask if he could be in a rock band, because he'd never been in a rock band."

The question in the pull line came after the first Gastr del Sol record was out.

eras.title: Jim and David
eras.text: For the next stretch Gastr del Sol was two people, David Grubbs and Jim O'Rourke, with John McEntire on the road. They made acoustic guitar records that came apart on purpose, one chamber piece, and records with violinist Tony Conrad.

years.h: Crookt, Crackt, or Fly gives The Sea and Cake its name
years.p: [[Sam Prekop|33175dbe-db6c-4f0b-a4c6-9addcd403186]]'s band [[The Sea and Cake|74171cb6-1ff8-42bd-be8a-96660c22e3e0]] named itself after mishearing the song title "The C in Cake". It's Gastr del Sol's first Drag City album, engineered by [[Brian Paulson|65f13d3b-ddd6-4b33-8ab7-366ee7fb63c4]] at Kingsize in Chicago.
years.xp: Two of its eight tracks, "Work from Smoke" and "The Wrong Soundings", run more than twelve minutes each; the closer is 14:49. [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]], Steve Butters and Gene Coleman on bass clarinet sit in.

years.p: A short Drag City follow-up to Crookt, Crackt, or Fly, released in 1994.

years.h: Grubbs guitars two songs on Codeine's The White Birch
years.p: [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]] plays on two tracks of [[Codeine|cecd5f91-cfdd-45d1-879f-3920c7c76e58]]'s second album, on Sub Pop.

years.h: The Harp Factory on Lake Street is named for a real factory
years.p: One 17-minute chamber piece, produced by [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] for Table of the Elements. The Lyon & Healy harp factory stands at Lake and Ogden in Chicago.

yt: Gastr del Sol live, The Point, Atlanta, Sept 23, 1995
years.h: Tony Conrad plays violin on The Japanese Room at La Pagode
years.p: Gastr del Sol also gives "Quietly Approaching" to the Red Hot AIDS benefit Red Hot + Bothered.

years.h: Upgrade & Afterlife closes on a John Fahey song
years.p: The closer is a [[John Fahey|95bb27d2-43c7-4a92-85ee-f95a245f0ee4]] cover with [[Tony Conrad|39b56aa8-5d36-49ab-ae5e-c3aa836b6620]] on violin. The opener's title is a cheap public-restroom perfume.
years.xp:
David Grubbs said Conrad got involved after a Gastr show in Atlanta, where he was "literally dancing with excitement" as [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] played the Fahey tune solo as an encore. The cover photo is Swiss artist Roman Signer's Wasserstiefel, water boots.

Reviews split hard: Alternative Press gave it five out of five, the NME four out of ten.

eras.title: Chamber pop, then silence
eras.text: The last album was the most tuneful, with strings, horns and a guest vocal. By that June, Grubbs and O'Rourke had stopped working together.

years.p: [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]], [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] and Oval's Markus Popp wrote it. [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]] drums and engineers, with [[Rob Mazurek|73c34525-f9c6-4c33-9abe-007748aaebe5]], [[Ken Vandermark|e5a4107f-5bb3-4f24-b9b7-927bb23840b5]] and singer [[Edith Frost|289faaeb-96bf-41ff-a15f-5166b6298e01]] as guests.
years.xp: Pitchfork put it at number 38 on its list of 1998's best albums. Fact later placed it tenth among the greatest post-rock records.

q: Jim, as the strong personality, kind of crowds people out of bands.
years.h: Grubbs and O'Rourke stop working together
years.p: By June 1998 [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]] had stopped working with O'Rourke. Wikipedia puts the split down to personal differences and grievances.
years.xp:
Grubbs told Paris Transatlantic that O'Rourke, the strong personality, tended to crowd people out of bands. The two also shut down Dexter's Cigar, their reissue imprint on Drag City, to make a clean break.

O'Rourke joined [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] the next year and went on to produce [[Wilco|9e53f84d-ef44-4c16-9677-5fd4d78cbd7d]]; Grubbs kept making records for Drag City and became a professor at Brooklyn College.

eras.title: Opening the archive
eras.text: Gastr del Sol never reunited on record, but the archive opened: first the Bastro tapes where it started, then a Gastr box nearly 25 years after the split.

years.h: Fourteen years on, Bastro's last shows get a release
years.p: [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]]'s Blue Chopsticks label puts out Antlers: Live 1991, the tapes where the first Gastr del Sol songs took shape.

years.h: A 3LP box lands nearly 25 years after the split
years.p: We Have Dozens of Titles gathers uncollected studio recordings and unreleased live sets on Drag City.
years.xp: Drag City lists it as a box of rare and unreleased studio and live recordings made between 1993 and 1998.
